issue_title: Allow students to send Q&A forum post notifications with no editing-time delay
issue_description:
allows students to send Q&A forum post notifications with no editing-time delay

new capability: 'canmailnow'

Description:

Currently, at the Moodle Forum, student posts will be sent after the global preset editing-time delay (30 min default) only. That cannot be changed at all. Neither by admins, managers nor by students.

As typical for a Q&A Forum, students are required to post once before viewing other students' posts. Then students have to wait for the whole preconfigured delay time before they can see the ongoing discussion. Especially for Q&A forums this can be an annoying experience.

Therefore, we suppose that it should be possible to enable students to decide themselves, with 'opt in' option, like teachers, to post an send notifications with no editing-time delay. This will improve students satisfaction and didactic meaning of this forums setting.

To decide self-sufficient and e.g. to fullfill individual security needs etc., Institutions, managers or teachers should be able to activate or deactivate the "Send forum post notifications with no editing-time delay" option for students.

*In our feature request this could be done by a low-threshold solution:* adjusting new users capabiltiy '{*}canmailnow{*}'.

A more convenient solution could be e.g. an activation within the course settings.

 

*Amendment* for editing and deleting (own) posts by students:

Students should be enabled  to decide by simple opt-in option to send QandA forum post notifications
 - with editing-time delay  -> editing or deleting possible until editing-time passed / other student post will be visible after editing-time passed

 - without editing-time delay  -> editing or deleting not possible anymore / other student post will be visible immediately.

 

To avoid cheating, once the post has been sent with no editing-time delay, it should no longer be possible to edit or delete that post by students themselves.

 

(ref forum discussion [https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=434324|http://example.com/])

issue_title: Move context classes to namespace
issue_description:
{color:#de350b}_*NOTE: this issue used to be about simplifying adding of new context levels, that is not the case any more, patch is now only refactoring of context classes*_{color}

-There are several use cases where it would be beneficial to allow easy creation of new context levels in plugins, for example Programs and Certifications.  Another example would a creation of cohort contexts.-

-In all use cases the main point is to allow delegation of management permissions at a more granular level than course category, for example assigning a role for adding and removing cohort members for one particular cohort without the need for a dedicated course category.-
h1. Implementation

All context level class were moved into \core\context namespace. To maintain backwards compatibility the old names were aliased in accesslib.php file, it was not done via standard core_component class renaming because the aliases will be kept for a long time without deprecation. I would not be reasonable to search/replace the whole codebase and all plugins now.

-Instead of hardcoding the list of available context levels in code there is a new file db/contexts.php which defines what context level classes are available in Moodle. This way plugins may add custom contexts without any kind of core modification while keeping similar performance.-

There are several new methods in context levels that allow new context levels to alter settings for default roles that are created during installation, another aim is to improve support for custom levels in permissions UI:
 # context::get_compatible_role_archetypes()
 # context::get_possible_parent_levels()
 # context::get_instance_table()
 # context::get_behat_reference_columns()

h2. Changes for end users

When importing data from external sources and in web services, numeric values of context levels can now be used instead of short context level names.
h2. Changes for developers

Normal code should not depend on actual PHP class names of context class, developers should always use numbers to identify context levels.

When dealing with external level identifiers developers should use new {{\core\context_helper::parse_external_level()}} method, which accepts both old short names and numeric context level values.

I have asked other devs if they like this proposal at [https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=435307]

issue_title: Add next and previous links on activity pages
issue_description:
I am creating this tracker, because I cannot find one that is created. So if this is double, I am sorry. 

This tracker is part of the discussion on Moodle forum [https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=433448|https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=433448)]

In this discussion the community points out that the removal of the module navigation button is causing issues with learners and teachers: 
 * Accessibility issues for relaying on tools to navigate through the course, they will have to go through sometimes a very long Course index.
 * Increases cognitive load for learners.

**/ updated 02-10-2023 -* *The need* 
As a student I want to navigate easily between the various activities in the same order as they appearing in the course index. 

 

*considerations*
 # navigation to be restricted to mod/xxxx/view.php?id= and not on  /course/view.php?id=xx&section=1 to avoid unwanted scenario's. 
 # text and media activity is not considered in this request. 
 # navigation should consider the module activity setting "make available but don't show on course page" and therefor not be part of the navigation as the teacher decided that it should not appear on the coursepage. 
 # Navigation during an Quiz or Lesson attempt might confuse students, suggestion would be to only show the navigation before starting the Quiz/Lesson and at the review page for the quiz/ end of the lesson.
 # navigation during the Book and/or H5P activity might confuse student, suggestion is to have a clear distiction between navigation within an activity and navigation that goes to the next/previous activity. 

* */* 

*Suggestion* 

Simple Next - Previous buttons at the bottom of a module page would be enough. To avoid issues with more complicated modules like H5P and Quiz, we  have good experience with having a 'small' line between the end of the module and the next/previous buttons. but normally don't encounter them if the space between the module and the buttons is 'width' enough. 
----
Edited to add:

Prior to Moodle 4.0, at the bottom of each activity page there were links to the next and previous activities in the course (following the order of activities listed on the course page). These links still exist for front page activities, as shown in the attached screenshot.

!previous, next and jump to menu.png!

Rafael explains the reasons for removing these links in his post [Re: Moodle 4.0 - Navigation between activities|https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=433448#p1756871].

For the future, it would be good to enable admins and maybe also teachers to choose whether or not to display next / previous links. Rather than adding another admin setting, an alternative way of achieving this would be to add a new capability to view next / previous links. This capability could then be allowed for the teacher and student roles at site or course level as required.

issue_title: Add team grading features to the assignment grade submission page
issue_description:
Assignment allows configuring team group submission to propagate both submissions and grades from one group member to the rest. However, the grading interface is not adapted at all to group submissions and has only individual student grading.

There are several ways the assignment grading page can help grading groups but more UX research is needed to design which is the best one. Some possible options are:
 * Add a fast way to go to the next student without a grading. When the teacher revaluates a group member the grading is propagated to the rest of the members so the next student without grading will be for sure from a group that is not yet graded.
 * Add some kind of filters to ignore any student without grading or only one member per group
 * Add some next/previous team that goes directly to one of the next group grading page.

The following image summarizes some possible locations for the different options:

There are some things not working smoothly if you use the group assignment:
 # When grading, you are only able to grade per student. Yes, there is an option to make sure the grade goes to all members of that group, but you still end up clicking 100 times through the grading screen to the 10 groups graded.

post_title: Quiz-related improvements for Moodle 4.1
post_description: There are at least three groups of people aiming to make significant quiz-related improvements in Moodle 4.1. The good news is that from what I have seen so far, all these changes are compatible and should fit together. My plan was to write a short post summarising all the work that is either underway or proposed. However, that turned out to be impossible. Here is a long post summarising everything! Q) The Question-bank-4.0 collaboration [Epic MDL-72752 ] This project , lead by Thomas, Luca, Antonia and I, and developed by Catalyst AU , delivered a lot of Question-bank improvements to Moodle 4.0, but there were still other ideas that we could not get done in time. They should be in Moodle 4.1. These items are all in development now, and getting close to completion. Q.1) Better searching of question in the question bank: You will be able search based on almost any information you can see about questions in the question bank listing (and qbank plugins will be able to add even more ways to search). [ MDL-72321 ] Searching questions will work like searching the course participants page, but better. Therefore, there is some prior development so that both places are based on a library of reusable search code. [ MDL-72509 ] Then, in the Quiz, random questions will be enhanced. Instead of the current limited options to pick randomly based on category and tags, you will be able to say, “pick questions randomly from these search results” for any question-bank search. This will make random questions even more flexible. Q.2) New Question-bank activity instead of fixed question banks [ MDL-71378 ] Previously, every course in Moodle had exactly a question bank, whether you wanted one or not. In future you will be able to choose if and where you want your question banks. This will make it easier to control who can access each one. There will also be more flexibility to use questions from shared question banks you have permission to access when building quizzes [ MDL-72322 ]. These changes should also finally fix two long-standing issues with backup and restore: MDL-41924 Minimise questions included with quiz backups (or duplication) MDL-69306 Duplicated quiz uses the same questions from the same question bank: can confuse teachers if they expect questions were copied too Q.3) Manage categories screen in the question bank will be improved [ MDL-72397 ] This is a relatively small change compared to the ones above, but it should be a nice usability enhancement for this part of the question bank. For example, moving categories around using drag-and-drop. O) The Open University [Epic MDL-74607 ] The people who pay my wages want some things in the quiz, and the good news is that most of the things they want are things that I know people here have been asking for years. Perhaps now they will finally get built! Currently these are just proposals, so please give feedback about the ideas, and whether you think the overall concepts are good. Later, I will post more details (once I have worked them out!) and we can discuss the details. Note these things are certainly advanced features. There will be no need for anyone to use them, and if you don’t need them, they should not get in your way (if we get the design right). O.1) Let one quiz generate multiple grades [ MDL-74610 ] In the past people have asked for this in different ways. For example, calculating the grade for each section of the quiz, or based on the question bank category each question is in, but these are all just variants of the same underlying requirement: Having a student’s attempt at a particular quiz lead to several grades in the gradebook. The Moodle gradebook can handle this. (If you are wondering, the only thing in standard Moodle which uses this option is the Workshop (peer assessment) activity, which gives you two grades (here is an example from the Moodle demo site of a 'Limerics' workshop) : We need to make it possible for the Quiz to use this gradebook feature. There are other related grading requirements I have seen people ask for here. One goes like this: “To pass this quiz, students need to get an overall grade of 70%, but also, they need to get at least 50% on questions 7, 8 and 9 combined”. I think that the changes we propose to make can solve this. If the quiz puts two grades into the gradebook, one “overall grade” and one “grade for questions 7, 8 and 9” then you can use gradebook calculations to work out the right final result based on those two. Since this can be done in the gradebook, we should not duplicate that type of logic in the Quiz itself. O.2) Allow the question numbers in the quiz to be customised [ MDL-74609 ] When I first heard this requirement, my reaction was “surely the quiz does not need this bit of added complexity?!”. However, over the last few months, I have been given enough examples where this makes a useful difference to the student experience. The requirement is the ability to change the default 1, 2, 3 question numbers to any other short strings that you like. Here is a mock-up: As well as being given examples (related to online exams) that convince me this is needed, I have also realised that it is technically easy to implement, and it can fit quite nicely in the UI (little edit-this pen icon by the number while building the quiz) so I now think this is worth doing. O3) Allow the teacher to force the language for one activity [ MDL-74608 ] This is not really a quiz feature, but at the OU, this is something we want for quizzes, and so I will mention it here. Currently Moodle has the option, to force the UI language for a particular course: We would quite like to have this option for activities as well as entire courses (probably added to the ‘Common module settings’ section of the form). What do people think about that? M) Moodle HQ UX team After the changes made in Moodle 4.0, the next priority for the UX team at HQ is all the activities, including Quiz. They are going to announce their own plans soon, so I won’t steal their thunder. However, I will say that I had a meeting with them yesterday morning, to get a sneak peak of what they were thinking of, and we had a really great discussion about that, and I am excited. One of their areas of focus is making it easier for teachers to build quizzes (which, you might say, is lucky, because the OU changes proposed above are going to add even more complexity 😉). N) Ideas no-one is planning yet, but ... Both the Moodle HQ proposals and the OU ones improve the page where you build the quiz. As well as the features currently planned, there are other ideas I know people want which shoudl become more possible with the new designs. (Even if they don't happen for 4.1, it would be easier to add them.) An option for whether to use the Summary page at the end of the quiz, where students can review their attempt before submitting. An option to display some custom text (instructions) at the top of the Summary page, if you are using it. (For example “Before submitting, we suggest you check that you have dotted all your ‘i’s and crossed all your ‘t’s.”) An option for whether to show the ‘intro’ page when you first go into the quiz, or not. (E.g. for a short worksheet-type quiz with no time limit, perhaps you just want students to go straight into answering the questions.) … Summary So, lots going on, and I just want to add a warning: At the moment, this is mostly just proposed work. What actually happens, and whether it happens in time for Moodle 4.1, remains to be seen. Also, the reasone for posting now is to get feedback, so please give your comments.

post_title: Notification Emails
post_description: Hi folks, Moodle currently (as of 4.x) supports that as soon as a badge is received, that a notification email is sent to the student, that just earned the badge the teacher/admin that created the badge Use case In our use case we have additional requirements for sending a badge notification. If a course is tought by several teachers, all of them should receive a notification when one of their students earns a badge. Notifications should sent out to a custom email address (of a role account in the organization that uses Moodle) to inform that the student earned a badge. This email can be used to trigger an additional automated process by the system that receives this email. Is there someone that has further input in the notification process? Possible solution A possible solution how to address the use case described above would be the following: Sending a badge notification to personel of a certain role is done be adding a new capability. This capability is enabled for teachers and non editing teachers by default. There needs to be an additional field that contains a list of email addresses that can be provided where to send the notification. That could be a database entry like badge.notificationemail. Migration process If it is worth the effort I also would propose to change the current setting and have a migration process during the update. Current setting: The database entry badge.notification contains a number that indicates whether a notification is sent, and in case of yes, at what frequency notifications are sent to the issuer. Proposed new setting: Keep the entry badge.notification, however, change the interpretation to whether send any notification and if so, in what frequency it's send. However the creator get the notification only if he has the capability inherited via the role management. Add a new entry badge.notification_email that contains a list of email addresses where the notifiation is sent to. Add a new capbility "moodle/badges:getnotification" During the migration process the following should happen: The new capability should be added and given to the roles Teacher, Non editing teacher. Go over all badges, check if the property/setting (db entry) badge.notification is > 0 (enabled). no -> do nothing yes -> check whether the creator is in a group that has the new cabability to receive notifications. If the creator is in such a group, do nothing. If the creator is not in such a group, take his email and add it to the new db property badge.notificationemail to make sure that he still receives notification after the migration process. Any further input for this proposal is highly appreciated. If you also have notes or suggestions not to the use case itself but the proposed solution, feel free to submit it here as well. Thank you in advance. Stephan

issue_title: Statistics to help identify not useful (rarely chosen) distractors in MCQ
issue_description:
This is an attempt to clarify my initial request from [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-48299|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-48299] which I admit was not clear enough.

I believe my request is related to using quizzes to identify misconceptions in a student population, so instructors can know how to teach surgically.

Definition: A useful (functional) distractor is an answer in an MCQ question that is wrong, but which students _believe_ is correct (and so some population chooses it regularly prior to instruction). It can be an indication of a student having a misconception, which is essential in making good MCQs. A great example:

*What causes the seasons on Earth?*
1. The distance between the Sun and the Earth varies as the Earth orbits the Sun.
2. The Earth's axis is tilted relative to its orbit around the Sun.
3. Seasons don't exist on Earth.

Because it's a known misconception, many people will choose answer 1.

Because it's _not_ a misconception, few if any people will chose answer 3.

Does Moodle 4 have statistics or recommendations to help quiz creators know that answer 3 is not a useful distractor? That is, over time of using this MCQ, we will see trend in statistics that students don't pick this answer. It's a statistic that is tied to the distractor (answer), not the question. Moodle would recommend removing this answer, as it's not a functional (useful) distractor.

Facility index and other statistics I have seen ([https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Quiz_report_statistics|https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Quiz_report_statistics]) appear to have a granularity of a question relative to a quiz.

To evaluate distractors, one needs statistics for *answers* in the question in a quiz that's given, say, at the start of a semester to assess students understanding of concepts.

I don't have Moodle 4, but I know that before class I will look at my students' quiz results on material they're supposed to know from the prerequisite class, and I can see when a functional distractor (spotting a misconception) is working. I will see some % of students have picked the wrong answer (it might just be 15%, but it's consistent every semester, and I teach to it to correct the misconception). I've been teaching for 20+ years, however. I know what many of the misconceptions are. It was not the case when I started out. I had really bad distractors (like #3) in my MCQs because I felt there had to be at least 4 answers, etc. Coincidentally, having at least 4 answers to make a good MCQ is a misconception!

I want a feature that will show/recommend _removing_ answers such as #3 above, even if it means I only have two choices in my MCQ. A 2-answer question (1/2 random chance) with only one good distractor is the same as a 3-answer question (1/3) with a bad distractor. This follows advice about how to write good MCQs. See [https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=257037&mode=1|https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=257037&mode=1] for more details and discussion. In my original feature request, I cited [https://bmcmededuc.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/1472-6920-10-85|https://bmcmededuc.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/1472-6920-10-85] as a reference to research about rarely selected distractors.

Such statistics can also be useful in validating MCQs as part of Concept Inventories, which require validating known misconceptions. When an instructor can give an MCQ before a course and see the % of misconceptions (again like #1 above), at the end of the course there should be improvement with the same questions. But what should be consistent in the feature I'm asking is that answers that RARELY are chosen over time are junk and should be eschewed and/or revised.

I'm not 100% of how it should look, but if over time an answer in an MCQ is *never* or *rarely* chosen, there could be a recommendation on the question level of "consider eliminating poor distractors" and when one drills down one can see which distractors are not popular.

ETA: [Here's a UML sketch|http://www.plantuml.com/plantuml/png/XOz1IyGm48Nl-HL3JofiGO-ULZoBoFRe9Pk-sc6JD6GcO17_ksbNMHUHlMGcyxvvoTkAsgmbU2C7Zibc6qXqzgXdPhSg8_SWXAGp1OGzifoFT9nwCHsh1-tKAeko4ngcJ8_Zn0xo6gzqeheJbOUP-afawxG2JH4CnKU8DDV6E6z5wAbuvUHnt7uf4EKfqeVv_25sYb3lH5AR3kzAzwIrr4dRjYVkwB2IRctFsG7ezzOT_ZeGnR94VHuUKeBDDZf8HJWgtf1_wHq7I7r744_wyeD_KZIt3MqsQrbINCBkslQc-SvXjeXz2VuB] from [https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=257037#p1114564|https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=257037#p1114564] explaining possible ways to keep the data.
post_title: Identifying non-functional (useless) distractors (choices) in Multiple-choice questions
post_description: I read up on how to make good MCQs and one very important point is to use as many functional distractors as possible . This is harder than it sounds. Something that would be easy would be to identify likely non-functional distractors . They are simply answers that few students chose. The papers I read suggest that eliminating them from MCQs is an effective way to improve question quality. I'm suggesting adding statistics to questions that would keep track of this data. Something simple would work. Each multiple-choice question in the bank has added metadata keeping track of the number of times a choice appears (numberOfAppearances) and the number of times it gets chosen (numberOfTimesChosen). Here's a domain model of the problem (not a database model): With this data, it would be very easy to identify questions that have non-functional distractors. I find this statistic much more useful to improve my questions than the current set of statistics that are at a "question" level only. Of course, editing the text of a Choice should effectively re-set the stats to 0. There might be other subtleties on how to handle the data based on use cases. Actually, modeling distractors as a separate entity (independent of questions) is interesting, since I often re-use the text. A good distractor (functional) is useful in several questions. I can see the question editor having a feature to "suggest" functional distractors from other questions in the same category, for example. But these are all features that require more work. The basic feature of calculating the efficacy of a distractor is a simple start.

issue_title: Allow admins to deactivate SEB templates even if used in existing quizzes
issue_description:
If a course containing a quiz using a SEB template is restored in a new moodle site that SEB template will be added to the system's SEB templates and becomes available to any new quizzes added from now on. Because of the way SEB works, that template is only useful for a given SEB version. Once an institution/student upgrades to a new SEB version that available template will no longer allow the student.
As an Admin, I should be able to hide/deactivate that template in the system so that an editing teacher can no longer select it for a new quiz.

 

Discussion: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=441090
post_title: managing Safe Exam Browser Templates
post_description: Hi all, As you know each SEB template configuration built using the SEB configuration tool can be used by the Moodle-SEB integration namely through the Browser Key setting. This key however depends on the SEB version, so since we adopt a new SEB version every school year we also need a new SEB template every year.(1) The way we do our roll-over every year is by having a new moodle instance so the course content is reused by backup and restoring from one year to the next.(2) If a given course contains a quiz using a SEB template and is restored into the new year the SEB template will be added to the system level and will be available to all new quizzes in the new instance (year) despite not being useful - because of (1). Since it's being used we are unable to delete it, change its name or hide it for new quizzes (feature not available). What do you reckon could be the best approach to avoid publishing deprecated templates in the new instance? Thanks in advance

post_title: Open course index when enrolling
post_description: When you enrol into a new course, all the topics in the course index on the left side are open. With long courses it makes quick navigation very tedious. I'm aware that once you open or close the topics, those settings are saved for the next session which is a neat feature. However, when you have a course with 40 topics (one year course) user probably don't want to close them all by hand. Here are some suggestions to resolve this problem: By default all the topics should be closed. Implement a functionality where the user can open/close all the topics. What do you think? Is there a reason why having all topics open at the beginning is the better option than having them closed?

issue_title: Badge notification to custom email addresses
issue_description:
At the moment when a badge is awarded the creator of that badge can be notified optionally. He then get an email notification about the user that got a badge awarded.

The proposal is here: instead of sending the notification to the creator of the badge, the email is sent to any email address that can be provided by the admin/creator. This solves the issue if the creator is not available anymore e.g. left the institution. Furthermore it allows notifications send to a role accout of the institution, e.g. a ticket system or similar that allows further handling of the awarded person. This could be for example adding/modifying user rights of the awarded user in some other system that might exist at the institution.

The topic has been discussed briefly at: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=439759

issue_title: LTI 1.3 Provider: warn user when launch omits ags claim or provides incompatible claim data
issue_description:
*Moodle versions:* 4.x

*LTI Provider:* 1.3/advantage + Grade synchronisation set Yes

*Background:*  In 2021 I posted an issue with LTI 1.1/1.2 Empty service url  ([https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=430048]) .

*Cause:*  We found out that this is due to a reset option on the LTI consumer side. This particular LMS implemented that the LIS_result_sourced_ids will be send without a the serviceurl because they don't expect a result back. 

*Moodle vs Moodle*
As posted in [https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=430048] I could not replicate this issue from Moodle - Moodle. 

*The problem we see:* is that when the LMS consumer is wrongly configured this is the reason why a grade is not being received.

issue_title: Quiz display options: make it possible to completely hide the grade information
issue_description:
h2. Background

Behind the scenes, the Moodle question system supports three options for what Mark information to display beside each question. These three choices can be seen when you preview a question in the quesion bank:
!Preview-options.png!

The three choices look like this:
!Not-shown.png!  !Max-only.png! !Mark-and-max.png! 

However, until now, the quiz has only made it possible to use two of those options for the questions in a quiz attempt:
 !Existing-quiz-options.png! 

Here, Marks off corresponds to 'Show max mark only', and on corresponds to 'Show mark and max.'

h2. Requirement

Pedagogically, there are situations were you want students to focus on the activity the quiz is getting them to perform, without any distracting thought about grades, and grade information is known to greatly distort students behaviour in some situations.

Also, sometimes, information about marks can provide meta-information which might help the student guess the right answer without knowing it. For example, if a multiple-choice, mulitple-response question is worth 3 marks, you might deduce that that you need to check three boxes.

So, we want to make all three of the Marks display options that the system is capable of available within the quiz.

h2. Proposed solution

Unfortunately, the only way we can think of to do this is to add another option, but at least this option fits consistently into the existing layout of the settings for, so hopefully this is not a massive increase in cognative load for teachers setting up quizzes. We will add a new Max marks option above the existing Marks checkbox. Marks will only be enabled, if Max marks is turned on. That gives the required three states:
 !New-setting-not-shown.png|thumbnail! !New-setting-max-only.png! !New-setting-mark-and-max.png!

When I [posted about this in the forums|https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=434473#p1748859] a while ago, the one serious response we got was in favour.

issue_title: MUA: Moodle Report Builder - Add Customizable SQL Functionality
issue_description:
*THIS IS AN MUA PROJECT PROPOSAL THAT WILL BE OR HAS BEEN SUBMITTED FOR POSSIBLE MUA FUNDING.  ANY EXISTING TRACKER ITEMS THAT THIS MIGHT DUPLICATE SHOULD BE LINKED TO BELOW.*  

*Note:* this project is being submitted by Ben Haensel and Gemma Lesterhuis. 

h3. Overview

The Moodle Report Builder gives us user the oppertunity to select a report source and build based on this resource a report. 

The number of report resources are increasing, though as admins we can receive user request to build a report that cannot be created based on the available resources. 

Currently admins use different ways to achive these goals, by example: 

# If you have access to the database directly from the database.
# Webservices functions calls to an external platform, if they are available for what you want to achive
# Plugins like  [configurable report|https://moodle.org/plugins/block_configurable_reports] and [SQL custom|https://moodle.org/plugins/report_customsql] 

h3. Why should we do this

As mentioned there are different ways in Moodle which admins can use to generated reports for their teachers. Though not all Moodle serviceproviders provided these options. MoodleCloud would be the best example, but there are many more. 

When it comes to plugins many of us rely on the community developers to maintain these plugins. As an example the configurable report block, maintained by 2 Moodle HQ employees has not been updated for a long time. Some serviceproviders will theirfor refuse to update the plugin because they are not sure if it's properly checked. As there is always a security risk in using plugins, especially a plugin that gives you peeks into the database, serviceproviders are very careful. 

When you use Webservices, the question then is if there is already a webservices available, and if not this should be build and as I stated above not all serviceprovider provide the option to install a 3th party plugin but also not all organizations that use Moodle have the budget to hire developers to do this. 

With launching the Report Builder in Moodle, alot of admins will now start using the provided templates. Even those who used the plugins before. But it is impossible to build a template for each userstory that an admin will encounter, look at the [current list of contributed ad-hoc reports|https://docs.moodle.org/310/en/ad-hoc_contributed_reports]. 

Which will mean that admins that build reports for the teachers (or other users) that can use alternative solutions will end up with having reports on different places. Which will make this more difficult to manage (also security wise) and confuses teachers on where they have to be for which report. 

Taking these reasons in mind, I believe it would be great if we could use the Moodle Report Builder functionalities to accommodate these reports. So that users will have access to their reports from 1 source, instead of using different methodes. 

*REAL LIVE STORIES FROM ..*

*Teacher*  - without knowledge of Queries

As a teacher I got access to a report that my admin build with the Moodle Report Builder. The admin explain to me how it works and. I like this feature and asked my admin to build me another report. My admin informs me he cannot build this report in the Report Builder since there is no template for it. 

When I searched Moodle.org/plugins I found this 3th party plugins, and asked my admin if he can use this. The admin confirms that knowledge of writting queries are available in the organization, but they are not allowed to install plugins nor do they have access to the database to create an alternative. 

*Supportdesk employee , role siteadmin* -with knowledge of SQL queries 

In our organization we use the LTI Publish course option. In our supportdesk inbox I found an email from a student that access the course through their own LMS. The student claims that they finished a course and did not receive the grade. In the course I can see that the student has indeed completed the course and there is a grade in the gradebook. As a site admin I can check the LTI grade sync task log, and I found that the grade has succesfully been send. Earlier we experienced problems with a different student, and we found out with help of our hostingsprovider that they had migrated to a different lms and we where communicating to the wrong serviceurl because this has not been updated. TO get this information I had to wait 2 days, because they had to check the database. I found with help of the moodle documentation which table I have to check. My hosting party prevents me to install 3th party plugins, as well have informed me that the 3th party plugins on moodle.org to have my Moodle version. Our organization budget is not that big, and each time I have to contact my serviceprovider I have to pay their fee. I noticed that Moodle Report builder is installed on my installation, though there is no standard report to check. What do I do? 

*Admin request to a serviceprovider*
I received the request from the organization to build a report. The Report Builder does not support this kind of report, as in there is no template. I do have the knowledge to write SQL queries. I ask my serviceprovider to install AdHoc Query Plugin because this is closest to my moodle version. I receive an email back for the serviceprovider that they don't install 3th party plugins on the Moodle Site. 

*Admin searching for alternative options*

As an admin I use Moodle 4.1 and really like the report builder, but I want to use an query that I found on the ad-hoc contributed reports|[https://docs.moodle.org/310/en/ad-hoc_contributed_reports|https://docs.moodle.org/310/en/ad-hoc_contributed_reports]]. I know that my serviceprovider does not allow me to install plugins from Moodle.org that don't support my Moodle 4.1 version. I don't have the budget to hire a developer to check the plugin, I want to use. They also denied the request for access to the database, so I can run the query myself. They replied they can run the query but this will cost me their consultancy fee. I know that I will use this query on regular bases and my organization cannot affored to pay for each request. I have been search the webservices but there is none that will help me along. 

Due to the restrictions of my servicesprovider I will have to discuss with management to migrate the site to a different provider, though I know that budget is an overal issue. 

*note: certainly more stories can be found, these are just a few I have encountered of the years.*

h3. Summary

* *Project size*: Large
* *Audience*: primary schools, universities, work places
* *Target users*: administrators

h3. Goals

# Create a report source called "SQL" so that admins can write a Select SQL query in an easy to use editor. 
# Create a premission so that Admins can grant the Report source SQL premission to users they trust and understand the functionality. 

h3. User Stories 

As an admin, I should be able to to call a report source called SQL so that I can write an SQL select query in the editor screen. It should not be possible to write a SQL query that updates or removes data from the database. 

As an admin, I should be able to verify the query which will ensures a check to see if the query can be runned by the database, if a query cannot be runned the error will show between the editor -en- and button. 

As an admin, I should be able to view the result of the query by clicking on a view result button. The query will be then shown between the editor in a table view. 

As an admin, I should be able to grant access to users by using the Report Builder Audience functionality so I can easily decided and control access over the report. 

As an admin, I should be able to schedule the report using the Report Builder Schedules functionality so I can email the report to the selected Audience.

As an admin, I should be able to see an overview of those I granted access using the Report Builder Access tab so I have a clear overview of the users.

As an admin, I should be able to grant an user premission to use the report Source SQL by adding the premission to the users system rol. 

As an admin, I want to see in the Moodle Security Checks report a 'warning' when users have the premission to create an SQL report with the Report Builder in a similar way as with the XSS trusted users and Backup of user data.

post_title: Useful SQL Queries?
post_description: I've been working on some queries recently, thought I'd share some of the ones that others may find useful. I'm also very interested to hear any thoughts on how I can improve my SQL . Im not the best at writing SQL so any advice will be much appreciated. This first one counts up the modules added to a given course, just change the course id number for "c_modules.course" in the WHERE clause... SELECT modules.name, COUNT(c_modules.id) AS "Module Count" FROM mdl_course_modules c_modules INNER JOIN mdl_modules modules ON c_modules.module = modules.id WHERE c_modules.course = 560 This next one produces a basic report with a row per course, counting the amount of students, student course views (hits) and the average view per student, a few other peices of data (such as the path and a few id's) are thrown in to make it useful within a web application. Also, you may wish to ignore the "TopLevelCatName", I store our cost centre codes in the category description field... SELECT y.TopLevelCatID, description AS TopLevelCatName, y.CategoryID, y.CategoryName, y.CategoryPath, y.CourseID, y.CourseName, y.Views, y.Students, y.ViewsPerStudent FROM mdl_course_categories cats INNER JOIN ( SELECT x.CourseID, x.CourseName, x.Views, count(*) AS Students, (x.Views/count(*)) AS ViewsPerStudent, TRIM(LEADING '/' FROM SUBSTRING_INDEX(x.CategoryPath, '/', 2)) AS TopLevelCatID, x.CategoryID, x.CategoryName, x.CategoryPath FROM mdl_role_assignments roles INNER JOIN ( SELECT course.id AS CourseID, course.fullname AS CourseName, count(*) AS Views, categories.id AS CategoryID, categories.name AS CategoryName, categories.path AS CategoryPath, context .id AS ContextID FROM mdl_course_categories categories INNER JOIN mdl_course course ON categories.id = course.category INNER JOIN mdl_log log ON course.id = log.course INNER JOIN mdl_context context ON course.id = context.instanceid WHERE log.module = "course" AND log.action = "view" AND context.contextlevel = '50' GROUP BY categories.id, categories.name, categories.path, course.fullname, course.id ) x ON roles.contextid = x.ContextID WHERE roles.roleid = '5' GROUP BY x.CourseID, x.CourseName, x.CategoryID, x.CategoryName, x.CategoryPath, x.Views ) y ON cats.id = y.TopLevelCatID ORDER BY y.CategoryName, y.CourseName

post_title: Global search performance
post_description: Hi all, we are using global search enabled and powered by solr. However a search takes quite a while until it results show up. Running a query against solr itself is pretty fast. Also, triggering the same query from the webserver against the solr server is fast. From within Moodle I did some meassurements. Solr itself doesn't seem the problem. A lot of time is lost in this function: `\core_search\manager::get_areas_user_accesses($limitcourseids, $limitcontextids);` A lot of things happen there where I am not yet fully aware of what it is. There's also a rather large SQL query about getting blocks within a course. In my serarches this didn seem matter much, the query was fast. My idea was that for every user the search usually returns the same contextids unless he uses a filter. So we could cache the result from that function for a few minutes (depending on the parameters). There I realized another problem, the contextinfo object contains arrays in the form of `[id => "id"]` , which bloats the array nearly to the double size, thus wastes too much memory in the redis (or whatever cache is used). From experience I know that there are performance differences when using `in_array($id, $array)` vs. `isset($array[$id])` (I don't know how the `array_key_exists($id, $array)` performs in this case). So, keeping the ids in the key and dropping the value seems a good solution only to discover that the values are used somewhere later (which would have to be changed as well). Doese any of you have search performance issues, and if so what are you doing to circumvent them? Thank you, Stephan

issue_title: Provide option to save question edits without creating a new version
issue_description:
See [Quiz forum discussion|https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=452158] for context

 

*Summary of problem*

The current format of the question versioning affects statistical reporting when minor corrections/amendments are made during or after a quiz assessment has occurred. In previous versions, if any errors leading to confusion or misunderstanding was encountered during or after a quiz assessment, facilitators were able to amend the question, the update would be immediately reflected in the quiz and the quiz statistics would be unaffected by the change. This is not currently happening on v4.1.5 as the change to a question updates the version, and even though the question is set to _Always the latest_ the update does not appear during an ongoing quiz and in the case of an edit to a question answer, the statistics only shows the stats for the users affected by the amendment.

 

*Suggestions*
 * When questions are edited, is it possible to give the user the option to keep the change within the current version of the question, while also updating current attempts, if the change is considered minor;
 * Alternatively, have the statistics reflect all attempts, if an amendment is made to 1 question.

 

Kind regards

Alex

issue_title: Reintroduce the option to set custom params at the instance level
issue_description:
In 4.3, we removed the ability to manually configure an External Tool instance. I.e. users cannot add an "External tool" instance from the activity chooser any more. They instead, must configure a site or course tool, and then use that tool to create resource links (using content selection, most likely).

This workflow is ok, provided the tool supports content item selection (deep linking). Which of course, is not the case for all tools, particularly the old 1.1 tools (in LTI 1.3/LTI Advantage, deep linking is part of the core suite of specs so most tools implement it in order to be certified).

We're seeing reports of tools which are using URL params to identify resources (e.g. tool.example.com?resource=123 or even the old Moodle provider code). [https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=454439].

Previously, the URL param would be entered in the instance form (in the tool URL field), and the tool could load that specific resource on launch. Teachers could paste in the URL, including the params, and it would launch that specific resource. This was a means of sharing access to the specific resource without deep linking too. 

Now, since we've nowhere to set that in the instance form, and more specifically no way to indicate a resource id at all (it's all hidden and tied into deep linking workflows), the only way tools like this (those which don't support deep linking) can create links is to create one tool PER RESOURCE, in the course tools page. This, of course, is hugely clunky and not practical at all.

This issue is not about re-adding the URL param support - we don't want to do that. Instead, it's about considering whether we want to surface the 'custom params' form field again, under an 'advanced fields' section of the form, so that teachers can enter the id of the resource - should the tool support loading the resource via custom params. This won't instantly solve the problem for tools like the above, which use URL params, but it does at least provide a proper avenue to set resource ids and the like, should the tool not support deep linking.


References:
MDL-78573 is the 4.3 Epic, but the form was locked for legacy tool instances in MDL-78597.
https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=450974#p1813411
https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=454439

post_title: Late quizzes with penalty
post_description: In this post, I present a simple workaround procedure for setting late penalties for quizzes. I have tried it with success for: Quiz Attempts allowed: 1 It may also work with other settings, multiple quizzes, etc. Pros The procedure does not require much more work from the teacher than would be required with a built-in routine if it existed. Students that are not late have nothing special to do. Late students have to declare their lateness in order to add time. References https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-4309 https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-8495 Example The example quiz is called "Quiz1" Due date: 15 September 10:00 am Penalty / lateness: 5% / 1 hour 10% / 1 day 20% / 2 days 30% / 3 days 40% / more than 3 days Procedure Use another small quiz called say "AddTime" and define the following settings for "Quiz1" and "AddTime". "Quiz1" settings Restrict access Hidden Student must match any of the following Date until 15 September 2017 10 00 or Student must match all of the following Date from 15 September 2017 10 00 and Date until 15 September 2017 11 00 and Grade AddTime ≥ 95%  < 96% or Student must match all of the following Date from 15 September 2017 11 00 and Date until 16 September 2017 10 00 and Grade AddTime ≥ 90%  < 91% or Student must match all of the following Date from 16 September 2017 10 00 and Date until 17 September 2017 10 00 and Grade AddTime ≥ 80%  < 81% or Student must match all of the following Date from 17 September 2017 10 00 and Date until 18 September 2017 10 00 and Grade AddTime ≥ 70%  < 71% or Student must match all of the following Date from 18 September 2017 10 00 and Grade AddTime ≥ 60%  < 61% "AddTime" question Student has to declare his lateness: Multiple choice question One or multiple answers? One answer only Choice 1 On time: 100% (Does not apply. May be hidden with <div style="position:relative;">) Choice 2 One hour late: 95% Choice 3 One day late: 90% Choice 4 Two days late: 80% Choice 5 Three days late: 70% Choice 6 More than three days late: 60% Penalty for each incorrect try: 0% "Add Time" settings Attempts allowed: Unlimited Grading method: Last attempt Restrict access Student must NOT match any of the following Hidden Grade Quiz1 must be ≥ (leave blank) must be < (leave blank) or Hidden Date until 15 September 2017 10 00 Grades Add a formula such as: Quiz1withLatePenalty =⟦Quiz1⟧*⟦AddTime⟧ Best regards,

issue_title: LTI Provider handling for Status Code 400+ errors
issue_description:
Moodle's LTI Provider component only logs errors from the sync members and sync grades tasks that integrate the Moodle LTI Provider with the Names & Roles Provider Service and Assignment & Grades Service on the platform (respectively).

This leads to a large number of unfulfillable requests to those services. A suggested improvement would be to:
 * Report error states in the Enrolment Method Menu
 * Stop (or delay) sending rejected requests from the platform if the status code semantics as defined by mod/lti indicates there is no expectation that the same request will ever be accepted
 * Provide an override button for that stoppage or delay to perform a service synchronization job on-demand

For those using the Moodle LTI provider with non-moodle platforms, it would be nice (but complicated and clunky) to be able to customize the error handling procedure in the Platform Registration menus.

issue_description:
One of our students contacted us because he could access his courses only via his user profile, but not via his dashboard. He couldn't understand why his dashboard was empty.
In fact he configured his dashboard to show his "future" courses instead of his courses "in progress".

issue_title: SCORM keep-alive aligned with session timeout
issue_description:
This enhancement is to address a situation that several of our clients encounter when deploying SCORM packages, and which is articulated in this [Moodle forum|https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=436346]:

_The user opens the package, walks away, comes back several hours later (without intervening Moodle or SCORM activity) and continues, and by then the Moodle session has timed out, so nothing is recorded back in Moodle... but it appears to the user that they've completed it._

The suggested solution is to leverage the existing "unstable connection" modal, so that closing out the modal forces a user back to the SCORM activity page. If session timeout has not yet occurred (because the communication failure is due to unstable internet connection), the learner can relaunch the SCORM; if timeout has occurred, the user will be directed to log in again.

*Acceptance criteria*
As a learner in a Moodle site, I will know this is done when:
 * I have launched a SCORM package in one of the following ways: 
 ** Standard window, in which the SCORM is embedded within the Moodle frame
 ** New window via Moodle SCORM setting, in which the SCORM is actually inside a 100% width/height iframe wrapped inside the _player.php_ file.

 * If communication between the SCORM package and Moodle fails—either because of unstable internet connection or a system timeout—I see a modal with the following message while in the launched SCORM package:
 ** "Due to an unstable internet connection or system timeout, learning progress is now at risk. To ensure your progress is saved, you should exit and relaunch this activity.”
 * The options presented to me by the modal will depend on whether I have experienced multiple communication failures during my user session:  
 ** If I am experiencing the first failure during my user session, the modal will display a choice of two buttons: 
 *** Continue (I remain in package)
 *** Exit (I relaunch package or, if system timeout has already occurred, log in to the site again)
 ** If I am experiencing a second consecutive failure in my user session, the modal will only display an "Exit" button. When I close the modal in any way (clicking "Exit," clicking the close button, clicking outside the modal) I am immediately redirected to the SCORM activity view.php page, which will force me to re-enter the SCORM activity before proceeding; if timeout has occurred, I will be redirected to the login page.

issue_title: LTI 1.3 Content Selection - 'Add to gradebook' should not be offered when grade sync is turned off
issue_description:
When grade sync is turned off on an activity (e.g. a quiz) in the tool, the option to 'add to gradebook' is still offered in the platform's content selection window. This is confusing for users who would reasonably expect to be able to add it to their gradebook if offered. 

As identified by Jake here [https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=462358] this behaviour is based only on whether the activity supports grading at the moment. The code can be found here: [https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/aea624fcb0229d40568850c9de808de2155d4beb/enrol/lti/classes/output/renderer.php#L88] 

Ideally, the content selection window would reflect whether grade sync is turned on for that activity, removing the option to 'add to gradebook' when turned off.

issue_title: LTI 1.3 Moodle <> Blackboard Quiz Results & Grade Sync Behaviour for Unattempted Quizzes
issue_description:
Kia ora koutou,

 

I just wanted to identify a recommended way to resolve the 'issue' whereby those (students) who do either A) do not attempt a quiz (i.e., do not open a quiz) or B) open the quiz and clicks 'Attempt Quiz' but does not provide any answers (come the due date of the quiz) do not send a zero mark via grade sync back to our core LMS.

 

Currently, if a student fits into either criteria A or B the grade sync does not send a zero grade from Moodle to our core LMS (Blackboard) as the grade sync logs note "Not sent - The grade for the user '###' in the tool '###' for the course '###' was not sent as the grades are the same."

 

I have had clarification that this behaviour occurs because whilst the quiz is still open the grade for the quiz is NULL; the sync grades task won't send any data when the student hasn't made an attempt yet. (Since [NULL !== round(0,5)|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/main/lib/gradelib.php#L1634])
When the due date closes on the quiz, the grade for the quiz changes from NULL to 0, and we see the "Not sent - The grade for the user '###' in the tool '###' for the course '###' was not sent as the grades are the same." message since the [lastgrade value it compares against to see if it needs to send a grade update is initialized to 0.00000|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/main/enrol/lti/classes/local/ltiadvantage/entity/user.php#L119], and they are now equal.

Moodle forum post on this topic: [https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=461004]

Note: this isn't limited to 4.3.#, this is just what we're currently using (4.3.8) and experiencing it on. I will note that this is expected behaviour (well appears to be from the above forum discussion) so will be experienced on all other versions).

 

What we'd like to happen is for the grade sync to send a zero grade once the due date closes for those who either A) do not start a quiz or, B) do start a quiz but do not provide any answers. 

We have the development team (one member being [~accountid:557058:ebbbbe18-eeb0-4474-9967-e279c8c00044]) to implement such a change and are happy to do so, but would like to agree on *what should* be done/{*}how should{*} this be done.

 

Many thanks in advance.
post_title: Quiz Results + Grade Sync Behaviour
post_description: The University of Otago is utilising Moodle for STACK question types, and because Moodle is not our main LMS (this is Blackboard), we use the grade sync feature to send Moodle quiz results back to Blackboard. This mostly works without issues, however, we have noticed a few scenarios where the grade sync doesn't behave as we'd anticipate. There are a couple of scenarios I have been able to test and rule out as to why the grades don't sync. However, there is one odd scenario that I hope someone can explain the behaviour(s) I'm seeing. What I am testing: A student who follows the LTI link from Blackboard to Moodle and then clicks 'Attempt Quiz' but does not provide any answers to the quiz. By clicking 'Attempt Quiz, ' they're added to the 'Results' section of the particular quiz (important for grade sync). The quiz then closes due to a due date passing. The student gave no answers. Results: 1.    Before the due date, the grade sync was not sending a grade as the submission was still in progress. The grade sync for this states: a.    Starting - Grade sync for shared tool '207' for the course '25'. b.    Skipping - Invalid grade for the user '591' in the tool '207' for the course '25'. c.    Completed - Synced grades for tool '207' in the course '25'. Processed 1 users; sent 0 grades. 2.    After the due date, the grade sync still has the same outcome, just a different reason (see line B) a.    Starting - Grade sync for shared tool '207' for the course '25'. b.    Not sent - The grade for the user '591' in the tool '207' for the course '25' was not sent as the grades are the same. c.    Completed - Synced grades for tool '207' in the course '25'. Processed 1 users; sent 0 grades. NOTE: at this point, if the student attempts to access the quiz again, they're shown a screen that states, ' Your final grade for this quiz is 0.00/2.00 ' and this 0.00 grade is also viewable in the 'grades' area of the course. 3.    I then manually overrode the 0.00 grade to… 0.00 and saved this. Yet still, the grade sync remains the same as point 2 above. 4.    I then overrode the grade to 1 (from 0.00). Sure enough, it worked: a.    Starting - Grade sync for shared tool '207' for the course '25'. b. Success - The grade '0.5' for the user '591' in the tool '207' for the course '25' was sent. 5.    I then overrode the grade back to 0.00 (from 1, which was 0.5 based on scaling within Moodle), and again the grade sync was successful a.    Starting - Grade sync for shared tool '207' for the course '25'. b. Success - The grade '0' for the user '591' in the tool '207' for the course '25' was sent. c.    Completed - Synced grades for tool '207' in the course '25'. Processed 1 users; sent 1 grades. So, I suppose I'm trying to understand why Moodle does not trigger the initial 0.00 grade (after the due date) to be sent in the first grade sync after the due date? Instead, Moodle continues to send the same grade as before to the due date (incomplete/in progress), yet the student can see their 0.00 mark in Moodle. Any guidance surrounding this would be much appreciated!

post_title: HEADS UP:  MNet support will end in Moodle 2.3
post_description: ADVANCE NOTICE: We plan to remove our proprietary MNet subsystem from Moodle 2.3 (planned for release in over a year, June 2012 ).  It causes us constant problems, is not well-defined, and only implemented by very few other systems. We plan to redesign the functionality completely, replacing it with standard web service functions, standard protocols and probably standard authentication schemes like OAuth 2.0. We want to work with the Mahara developers (and anyone else who may be using Mnet) to ensure a smooth changeover, but it's unlikely that the new system can be directly backward-compatible with MNet. This means that if you use MNet in a significant way, you need to upgrade all your networked systems at the same time and reconfigure the networking. At this stage the design for the new systems is not defined at all.  My own thinking is that we should think holistically about how Moodle can share authentication and the old MNet services with all kinds of other systems, not just Mahara.  If you have any ideas on what we should do and how, then now would be a good time to start brainstorming!

issue_title: Activities restrict - better detect From/Until choices
issue_description:
As shown here : [https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=465563]

Being able to use many "From" or "Until" in the activities restrictions (when NOT nested) leads to conflicting parameters and potential errors that are not automatically detected as such.

Example in attachment.

Improvement: 
There should be a possibility to detect the use of more than one "From" and more than one "Until" inside one set of restrictions (maybe it makes sense when restritions are nested for specific use cases)  and flag it as a potential conflict.
post_title: Activity restrict and choices from/to (bug/improvement)
post_description: Hi everyone, Instructional designer in a university here (and manager of Moodle platforms for a few years). My first comment will be about an issue we faced during recent exams, due to the ways activities could be restricted. I haven't found a similar concern here for now, so here it is. Platform: Moodle 4.1.15+ Context : A few days ago, I had to replace an exam subject in a hurry a few moments before it started. The mistake I made: As I was in a hurry, I used the activity restrictions inappropriately: Instead of restricting my activity " From xx/xx/xx Until xx/xx/xy", it ended up being " Until xx/xx/xx Until xx/xx/xy" (image below). The consequence: The exam subject was not available, and this error was not easy to detect. The exam had to be delayed for ~15min, and this caused a lot of unnecessary stress to lots of students. Reproduction: I managed to reproduce the problem on a fresh Moodle install (4.5.1). Improvement: There should be a possibility to detect the use of more than one "From" and more than one "Until" inside one set of restrictions (maybe it makes sense when restritions are nested for specific use cases)  and flag it as a potential conflict. I hope that my first contribution will be worthwhile. Thanks for reading!

issue_title: Moodle 5 shared question banks: no way to move questions from a course-level bank into a quiz
issue_description:
As first reported in this Moodle Quiz forum post [https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=466039] , there is a regression issue with the Question Bank/s architecture in Moodle 5 development version (and probably the [latest] Moodle 4.6 as well). 

In Moodle 5 (last tested on the QA site '5.0dev (Build: 20250214)' on 2025-02-18), it is not possible to move questions "down" - from a course-level Question Bank to a local Quiz-level Question Bank.

This is because in the Quiz context the Questions and Categories view pages NO LONGER list higher level Question Banks, not even for the Admin.

The current solutions only allow the Teacher to move questions "up" - from the Quiz level to the Course level, using the "With selected" > "Move to" and then selecting a higher-level QB, including the course level (and also the category and system levels if you're an admin), but never in the opposite direction from course to quiz.

This new limitation is unfortunate especially since "localising" questions has been one a most effective way of minimising needless duplication of course-level questions and categories when importing courses, as well as a good way of protecting questions from being needlessly shared with other quizzes in a course. I also simply believe that the Move questions option should remain bi-directional, as before. Perhaps some version of a "Switch bank" button, available in a Quiz's add question from question bank modal page, could be added on the Quiz > Question Bank > Questions sub-page to bring back the lost functionality?

I provide screenshots taken during tests performed on my local Moodle 5 installation a few days ago:

post_title: Moodle 5dev: Impossible to move questions from a course-level Question Bank to a local Quiz-level question bank
post_description: Dear Tim and Quiz / Question / Question Bank Developers, I seem to have hit a regression issue with the new Question Bank/s architecture in Moodle 5 development version (and probably the [latest] Moodle 4.6 as well). To put it briefly: In Moodle 5 ('5.0dev (Build: 20250206)'), after I add a Quiz to a course and then add questions to its local Question Bank, I am able - if needed - to move these questions to the higher course level Question Bank by selecting them and choosing "With selected" > "Move to" and then selecting a higher-level QB, including the course level (and also the higher category a system levels if you're an admin): HOWEVER, moving questions in the opposite direction - from a course-level Question Bank to a local Quiz-level QB - seems impossible now. This is apparently because in the Quiz context the Questions and Categories view pages do NOT list higher level Question Banks branches, not even for the Admin (at least by default?): And, of course, a it's always been, from a course-level Question Bank it is not possible to select questions and move them to a quiz-level question bank. This new limitation would be most unfortunate especially since "localising" questions has been one a most effective way of minimising needless duplications of course-level questions and categories when importing courses, as well as a good way of protecting questions from being needlessly shared with other quizzes. I also simply do believe the Move questions option should remain bi-directional, as before. I would consider this a regression bug, therefore, since we're losing functionality here, and be inclined to start a tracker issue for it, but wanted to first mention the problem here on the forum. Thanks for any responses and comments. Kind regards, Przemek

post_title: HEADS UP:  MNet support will end in Moodle 2.3
post_description: ADVANCE NOTICE: We plan to remove our proprietary MNet subsystem from Moodle 2.3 (planned for release in over a year, June 2012 ).  It causes us constant problems, is not well-defined, and only implemented by very few other systems. We plan to redesign the functionality completely, replacing it with standard web service functions, standard protocols and probably standard authentication schemes like OAuth 2.0. We want to work with the Mahara developers (and anyone else who may be using Mnet) to ensure a smooth changeover, but it's unlikely that the new system can be directly backward-compatible with MNet. This means that if you use MNet in a significant way, you need to upgrade all your networked systems at the same time and reconfigure the networking. At this stage the design for the new systems is not defined at all.  My own thinking is that we should think holistically about how Moodle can share authentication and the old MNet services with all kinds of other systems, not just Mahara.  If you have any ideas on what we should do and how, then now would be a good time to start brainstorming!

issue_title: Create layout for LTI course publishing which excludes site nav
issue_description:
I have a course hosted on a [MoodleCloud|https://moodlecloud.com/] site (the 'Tool' in LTI 1.3 speak) that is accessed from a customer's self-hosted Moodle (the 'Platform') as a course-level LTI activity.

When displayed on the Platform site, when logged in as a student the Moodle header bar (Home / [Dashboard|https://moodle.org/mod/glossary/showentry.php?eid=10485&displayformat=dictionary] / My Courses etc) from the Tool site is still displayed so the student can navigate out of the course. I gather the correct behaviour is that this header bar should only be displayed for teacher and admin users logged in with LTI, but for students it should not be displayed. 

I can use the force_embed=1 configuration in the LTI Tool settings on the Platform to hide the header for ALL users, however that's not ideal as this method also removes not just the site header bar but also the course left navigation block and course user menu, all of which should be retained for the student. 

 

Response from Jake Dallimore in Forums was as follows:

_Hi Mark,_

_You've just discovered a long standing limitation and perhaps a good candidate for future improvement._ 

_With published [activities|https://moodle.org/mod/glossary/showentry.php?eid=54&displayformat=dictionary], we force the page layout to embedded for student launches, and this works fine. With courses, we don't do this (we never have, even going back to before I ported the tool/provider to LTI1.3) so we'll fall back on the default 'course' layout in those cases (and yes, the header is shown in the course layout). [FYI|https://moodle.org/mod/glossary/showentry.php?eid=7471&displayformat=dictionary], you can see layouts here: [https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Page_API#Base_theme_page_layouts]._

_I think, ideally, we'd have a layout that we could use for course publishing, which excluded site nav, but I don't think a layout like that exists yet. Might be one to create a tracker issue for (using "Publish as LTI tool" as the component, if you do)._

_Cheers,_
_Jake_

issue_title: Support Site menu activities block in Single Activity format
issue_description:
The Social and Single activity course formats {*}share significant similarities{*}. However, [feedback from the forums|https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=452916] regarding a potential merge highlighted two key {*}user concerns{*}:
 * The *Social activities block* is exclusive to the Social course format, limiting the Single activity format to just one activity.
 * The Single activity format *automatically hides any additional activities* within the course.

Addressing these limitations could allow the {*}Single activity format to replace the Social format{*}, potentially reducing the number of core plugins.

 

Resolving this issue will improve the Single activity format by:
 * Ensuring that additional activities remain visible
 * Adding support for the Site main menu block.

This will then allow for the re-evaluation of MDL-79916, with the potential to remove the Social course format and the Social activities block.

issue_title: Multi-language support for additionalhtmlfooter
issue_description:
We are using additionalhtmlfooter to add additional info in multiple languages to the footer (the circle with the question mark on the bottom right of the page).
Unfortunately additionalhtmlfooter  does not render multilang.

It would make sense to be able to use multilang syntax in additionalhtmlfooter, as everything else behind the questionmark button is multilingual.
For multilang language support in the footer, text in Moodle's additionalhtmlfooter setting should get put through format_text().

Support for multilang in additionalhtmlfooter could be added in function standard_end_of_body_html() in lib/classes/output/core_renderer.php by replacing the line
$output .= "\n" . $CFG->additionalhtmlfooter;
with
$output .= "\n" . format_text($CFG->additionalhtmlfooter);

A discussion on Moodle.org forum can be found here https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=446795

issue_title: Allow OAuth2 login without a sesskey
issue_description:
Various SSO methods often have a concept of ‘autologin’ or ‘forced’ login, eg auth_saml2 has a mode for autologin and also for passive login where it can attempt a login to see if you are already logged in or not.

auth_oidc in core also has similar features to allow auto login.

auth_oauth2 by comparison does not only not have this feature, but its quite difficult to workaround this lack of a feature because there are no urls that ‘just work’ because they are protected by sesskey.

There are various forums pages asking for this with no real resolution:

[https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=432803|https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=432803]

[https://stackoverflow.com/questions/69610220/hide-moodle-default-login-page-and-use-oauth2-authentication-only|https://stackoverflow.com/questions/69610220/hide-moodle-default-login-page-and-use-oauth2-authentication-only|smart-link] 

I would propose that we simple remove the sesskey check here as the simplest fix:

[https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/main/public/auth/oauth2/login.php#L33|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/main/public/auth/oauth2/login.php#L33|smart-link] 

and remove the sesskey from the url here:

[https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/main/public/auth/oauth2/classes/auth.php#L183|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/main/public/auth/oauth2/classes/auth.php#L183|smart-link] 

Then you can set

{noformat}$CFG->alternateloginurl ='/auth/oauth2/login.php?id=x';{noformat}

And then we can layer extra settings on top of this, eg to make a specific oauth2 issuer the default forced login like we can with other auth plugins.

issue_title: Have a possibility to set a default question bank for a quiz
issue_description:
Looking at various Forum threads (as [https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=469674|https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=469674] (“Moodle 5.0.1 Question Bank”) or [https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=469819|https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=469819] (“M5: Can anybody please stop question bank?”)), it seems that:

# Having separate question banks for separate quizes being the default place for questions (new in version 5) is annoying to “advanced” users.
# Having only a single question bank for the whole course might be confusing for “inexperienced” users, when they duplicate a quiz for the first time.

I think that possibility to set a default question bank for a quiz (in the quiz settings) might be a mostly acceptable compromise, greatly decreasing annoyance for “advanced” users (hopefully, after setting the default question bank, things would work as before, with ability to ignore the separate question banks) without making things more confusing for the “inexperienced” users (the default option would be to have the separate question banks as default for new quizes).

Of course, ideally there would also be a way to set the default question bank for all quizes in the course and to set the default question bank for all new quizes in the course (probably in the course settings), but those would probably be the next steps.

Oh, and this differs from [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-86563|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-86563|smart-link], as in this case the default question bank would be set “forever”, not just for a single session.
post_title: Moodle 5.0.1 Question Bank
post_description: Hi everyone, We've recently upgraded to Moodle 5.0.1 and noticed that when creating questions directly inside a quiz, they no longer get added to the course question bank. This is a big change from previous versions where quiz-created questions were also stored in the course-level bank, making them reusable across other quizzes. We understand that the new structure distinguishes between quiz-level and course-level question banks, but removing the option to automatically store new questions in the course bank seems like a step backward in terms of usability . Wouldn't it make sense to at least provide an option to move or copy questions from a quiz context to the course question bank? This would help avoid duplicating work when building centralized or cumulative assessments. Is there a rationale behind this design decision, or is there a setting or plugin that can restore the old behavior? Thanks in advance for any insights!

issue_title: MFA: Factor email will not work if server is in private network and GeoLite-DB is used
issue_description:
Dear Community,

I posted on the Moodle forum a few days ago ([https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=470113),|https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=470113),] but haven't received a reply. I suspect this may be a bug, which is why I am opening a tracker entry here.

We are using Moodle 4.5.5+ (on PHP 8.1.33, CentOS Stream 9) in a private network (10.xx.yy.zz) and try to activate Moodle Core MFA with factor "email".

First we got this error message: "Error The address 10.xx.yy.zz is not in the database". I can press "next" and then I can access the form field where I can enter the 6-digit code, but I don't receive the code via email.
We are using IP address lookup and use a local GeoIP-City-Database (GeoLite2-City.mmdb). We think that the problem occurs because the IP address lookup could not resolve the IP address range 10.xx.yy.zz. If I don't use the GeoLite2-City-Database we don't get the error message and the code will be sent via email.

There was a similar problem with the former MFA Plugin set: [https://github.com/catalyst/moodle-tool_mfa/issues/444|https://github.com/catalyst/moodle-tool_mfa/issues/444|smart-link] 
I assume that the problem should also be solved in the core version, but maybe not?

One more thing: this issue might not happen with all Moodle installations that are in a private network. We think it happens if the mail server, which is used to send the email authentication infos to the user, is also in a private network.

thanks & best regards
Anton
